A1.justification: The differently titled PDFs describe the same xKG study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original PaperBench agent evaluations, node ablations, code-quality experiments, and a replication case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds graph-quality evaluations, comparisons with expert annotations, construction-cost measurements, and corpus-expansion results.

M1.justification: The graph structure, corpus-search stages, extraction/modularization/filtering pipeline, self-debugging, and final verifier are retained. The construction prompts match after moving from Appendix C to E. The paper-aware terminology and corpus expansion do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds construction scenarios for bridging-data-gaps and sample-specific-masks, expanding the corpus from 42 to 56 papers and adding model-adaptation/efficiency coverage. The five-paper replication evaluation remains unchanged; no downstream replication scores are reported for the additional targets.

E2.justification: v2 adds expert-constructed HumanKGs as reference comparators for automated graph construction on CFDG, RND, and TENT (Table 8). The agent comparators and the four code-quality configurations remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations assess technique validity, code executability, and technique-code agreement (Table 3). Appendix B.2 samples three papers for expert annotation and introduces weighted precision, recall, and F1 comparisons. The existing PaperBench evaluator, task settings, and agent runtime limits are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial direct analysis of graph construction: human quality checks, filtering errors by category (Figure 3), executability before and after self-debugging, agreement with expert annotations, and decomposition granularity. The original node ablations, code-quality experiment, case study, and target-paper failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report best@3 results in Table 1 and three runs for the same Figure 2 boxplots. v2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its new evaluations.

E6.justification: The existing replication scores, ablation scores, and performance plots are unchanged. v2 adds validity rates of 89.44%, 100.00%, and 74.51% (Table 3), reports executability rising from 52.38% to 100% through self-debugging, and gives weighted F1 scores of 0.95/0.89/1.00 for CFDG/RND/TENT (Table 8). Construction costs and corpus statistics are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The graph equations and node/edge definitions remain substantively equivalent, with no new assumptions, proofs, or derivations. v2 removes the preliminary task/score shorthand R=A(P) and S=E(R,T), but retains the same repository-generation task and weighted-rubric scoring description in Sections 3.1 and A.1.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an automated, extensible representation linking scientific techniques to executable code and improved replication across three agents and two LLMs, including the same 10.9-point gain. The revised emphasis on paper-aware updating develops v1's existing automated, scalable corpus-construction claim.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes technique-code mismatches mainly to overly broad snippets and argues that their application impact is small. It also explains variable decomposition as preserving methodological structure and construction expenditure as supporting repeated reuse. The existing target-paper failure explanations and Limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds third-party API disclosure and stage-level call, token, and cost accounting. It specifies ten combined relevant papers where v1 specified five selected references plus unspecified web results, without establishing a procedure change. Prompts and hyperparameters match, but shortened captions omit Table 2's explicit five-paper averaging and the case study's IterativeAgent attribution.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wu et al. (2024) to contextualize sensitivity to irrelevant information and removes the Burns et al. (2022) and Hua et al. (2025) references. The principal comparisons with earlier research systems and the distinction from ExeKG remain.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the central motivation, construction/integration exposition, analysis discussion, and conclusion around paper-centric representation. It removes the Preliminary subsection and reorganizes the appendices, placing construction analysis before target-paper analysis and the storage example before the unchanged prompts.

P2.justification: v2 adds the quality table, filtering-error figure, and cost/domain/expert-comparison tables. It revises Figure 1's labels and caption, redraws the existing case-study illustration, relabels Figure 2's full method as '+ Verify', and consolidates the configuration tables. The performance-gain plot and storage example are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The new human checks, expert-annotation comparison, and cost breakdown provide direct support for graph quality and practicality that v1 lacked. These benefits outweigh the small losses of caption detail. The gain is limited because the expert comparison covers three papers, annotation and weighting procedures remain underspecified, and downstream replication evidence is unchanged.
